title: New hire friction map and 90d retention playbook
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures common friction points new hires encounter at Redwood Inference during the first 90 days, and prescribes a lightweight, operational playbook to improve early retention and ramp velocity. Usable by hiring managers, people ops leads, and onboarding mentors.

Scope and intended audience:
- Scope: cross-functional onboarding (eng, product, SRE, solutions) focusing on the first 90d signals that predict attrition or slow ramp. Includes preboard -> day 1 -> week 1 -> month 1 -> month 3 actions.
- Audience: hiring managers, onboarding mentors, people ops partners, recruiting ops.

Design principles (how to use this):
- Prioritize friction of highest impact (blocking work or psychological safety).
- Lean runbook: try a single mitigation per friction point first; instrument and iterate.
- Make actions ownerable and timeboxed.

Friction map (observed, ranked by severity):
1) Access gaps (most common / highest impact)
   - Symptoms: delayed seat, missing cloud creds, no repo access, blocked CI token.
   - Consequence: cannot complete first PR or shadow pairing within week 1.
   - Quick fixes: 48-hour access SLA, check-list gate before D-1, buddy does a manual access sanity check on D0.

2) Role clarity mismatch
   - Symptoms: job description not aligned with first 30 day assignments; overlapping stakeholder expectations.
   - Consequence: new hire spends time guessing priorities; managers assume knowledge.
   - Mitigation: deliverable-oriented 30-day plan (3 small deliverables) shared on hire packet and read out on D1.

3) Mentor/manager misalignment
   - Symptoms: mentor gives tactical help while manager expects independent delivery; conflicting feedback.
   - Consequence: frustration, lower confidence, deferred decisions.
   - Mitigation: 15-minute mentor/manager sync on D0 and weekly 1:1 alignment note.

4) Onboarding overload (information dump)
   - Symptoms: 10+ docs, multiple tooling walkthroughs in first 2 days.
   - Consequence: cognitive burnout, low retention of critical info.
   - Mitigation: tiered docs (must-know vs nice-to-know), ‘day 1, day 7, week 4’ microlearning checklist.

5) Missing social integration
   - Symptoms: no intro to cross-functional peers, empty calendar, no team rituals exposed.
   - Consequence: slower trust formation, lower belonging.
   - Mitigation: calendarized 30-min intro slots for first 2 weeks; optional coffee pairs program.

6) Early task ambiguity in cross-pool dependencies
   - Symptoms: task requires infra changes owned by another team; no clear requester.
   - Consequence: blocked tickets, perceived slow progress.
   - Mitigation: pre-identified cross-team touchpoints and a templated request ticket for first cross-team ask.

Minimum success signals (what success looks like at each milestone):
- D0: seat + essential creds validated, manager + mentor assigned, first-day 30min sync completed.
- Week 1: first small deliverable or meaningful shadow session started.
- Month 1: three deliverables completed or clear progress on primary project; initial 30-day review conversation.
- Month 3 (end of probation): measurable contributions accepted to main repo, independently handling 1 recurring on-call or runbook task (if role requires), manager recommends continuation.

90d retention playbook (operational runbook)
Preboard (D-7 to D-1):
- Recruiter: send tailored hire packet containing 30-day deliverables, org chart, and required preboarding tasks.
- IT/Security: pre-provision minimum seat (email, slack, core cloud read-only) and track via ticket (internal SLA: 48 hours).
- Mentor: reach out with welcome note, schedule D0 coffee + week1 pairing.
- Manager: prepare a 30-day deliverable list and a 1-page success rubric.

Day 0 (first day):
- 9:00 AM: Welcome intro (People Ops) — 20 mins: benefits, payroll, basic policies.
- 10:00 AM: Team welcome with intros and 30-min show-and-tell of team goals.
- 11:00 AM: Mentor pairing and access sanity check (mentor to run through checklist).
- Afternoon: First small sandbox task assigned (no cross-team deps).
- End of day: Manager sends clarity note summarizing priorities for week 1.

Week 1 (days 2–7):
- Mentor shadow + pairing: 1–2 sessions (60–90 mins total).
- Recruiter/People Ops checkin at day 3 (async pulse via form).
- Deliverable: complete a small PR or documentation edit.

Weeks 2–4 (month 1):
- Weekly 1:1: manager and mentor meet with new hire to surface blockers and calibrate feedback.
- First 30-day review: manager uses provided 1-page rubric; focuses on signals not judgments.
- Social: schedule two cross-team 1:1s.

Months 2–3 (ramp and retention):
- Growth of responsibility: hand off a recurring task or small feature end-to-end.
- Manager does a mid-probation 60-day check-in and updates success rubric.
- People Ops triggers stay interview at day 45 if any negative signals in check-ins.

Mentor rotation and fallbacks:
- Default mentor length: 8 weeks.
- If mentor bandwidth issues arise: automatic handoff to backup mentor (identified at hire).
- Escalation path: unresolved blocker for >7 days -> manager -> EM lead -> People Ops partner.

Interview rubric (quick reference used by hiring managers):
- Technical calibration: ability to ship small, test-driven changes; evidence: linked PRs or take-home.
- Collaboration: cross-team communication and code review etiquette.
- Problem solving: clear breakdown and step plan; favors shipping over perfect design.
- Role fit/level: clarity about expected autonomy and examples of prior similar scope.
- Scoring: 1–5 scale with mandatory written evidence for scores <=2.

Probation success signals (to measure at 30/60/90):
- Observable outputs: PRs merged, runbook edits, bug fixes.
- Behavioral signals: asks clarifying Qs, proactively schedules syncs, accepts feedback.
- Self-reported confidence and manager-rated growth.

Measurement and instrumentation (KPI suggestions):
- Time to first merged PR (target: <=14 days for eng roles).
- Percent of hires with all D0 access by first work block (target: 95%).
- New-hire NPS at day 14, day 45, day 90 (goal: +40 at day 90).
- 90d retention rate (baseline and improvement target).

Unresolved questions / hypotheses to test:
- Hypothesis: a 30-minute mentor/manager D0 sync reduces 14-day friction by 30%. Proposed A/B test: randomize hires into D0-sync vs no-sync cohorts.
- Question: is 8-week mentor assignment optimal for mid-level engineers? Try alternate 4/12 week pilots for different levels.

Tactical templates (copy-and-paste):
- Manager D0 clarity note (template):
  "Hi {name}, welcome! For your first week please focus on: 1) repo setup and small sandbox PR due by Friday, 2) attend X pairing, 3) optional deep-dive session on the serving runtime on Wed. I'll meet you Mon 4 PM for a 30-min plan. -{manager}"

- Mentor D0 checklist:
  1) Confirm Slack + email + repo access.
  2) Walk through dev seed task and ensure it runs locally.
  3) Add new hire to 1–2 calendar rituals.
  4) Schedule pairing sessions for week 1.

- Preboard ticket checklist (to be used by recruiting ops):
  - Laptop order placed (specs: Macbook Pro M1-like or cloud dev kit)
  - Core email + Slack created
  - Cloud console (read-only) and code repo access staged
  - Benefits enrollment link sent

Quick wins (low effort, high impact):
- Mandate D0 mentor/manager 15-min alignment meeting.
- Ensure one calendar event block reserved for "first-week pairing" in template team calendar.
- Add a short one-page success rubric to every offer packet.

- Granularity of first-week deliverables by level (IC1 vs IC3).

End of doc.
